sentences.text: It has been asserted in the prosecution story that the victim and her sister got separated from their parents at the age of three years and a Muslim family of Kankarbagh Police Station area provided them shelter.
It is alleged that for the last three years the family under whose care victim and her sister were living also got separated and from the last three years they were living with the appellant.
It is alleged that appellant abused the victim physically and also raped her.
It is further alleged that despite having knowledge of the said act family of appellant did not help the victim.
Appellant tried to abuse victim's younger sister physically for the last one year.
It Patna High Court CR.

APP (SJ) No.3539 of 2024(11)
dt.08-09-2025 is alleged that victim and her sister made complaint to teacher who contacted voluntary organization.
It is further alleged that on the basis of aforesaid allegations, appellant was apprehended from meat shop.

4. On the basis of written report, instant case was registered under Sections 376, 376 C(A), 354(A),
344, 363, 370, 370(A) of IPC and Section 04, 06, 08, 10 of the POCSO Act and Section 75 of the Jevenile Justice Act and after investigation charge sheet was submitted under Sections 376,
376C(A), 354(A), 344, 363, 370, 370(A) of the IPC and Section 4, 6 and 10 of POCSO Act and Section 75 of Juvenile Justice Act and cognizance has been taken under Sections 376, 376C(A),
354(A), 344, 363, 370, 370(A) of the IPC and Section 4, 6, 8 and 10 of POCSO Act and Section 75 of Juvenile Justice Act and charges have been framed under Section 376, 376C(A) of the IPC and Section 6 of the POCSO Act.
5.
Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that appellant is quite innocent and has committed no offence as alleged in the FIR.
He further submits that appellant has provided shelter to abandoned girls.
He further submits that DNA test was conducted but the said DNA test denied the allegation levelled against the appellant in the FIR as appellant Patna High Court CR.

APP (SJ)
No.3539 of 2024(11) dt.08-09-2025 is not in any way connected with the alleged occurrence.
He further submits that there were nine persons residing in the same house which had only three rooms and, hence, the said occurrence cannot be possible.

He further submits that, despite the victim having already made allegations in the FIR that other persons, who are family members of the appellant, were well aware of the occurrence, they have not been made accused in the present case.
He further submits that appellant is in custody since 17.03.2019 .
He further submits that substantial portion of custody i.e. about six years and six months out of ten years, have already been elapsed and the appeal is not likely to be taken up in near future.

6. Learned counsel for the State has submitted that the victim has specifically made accusation against the appellant who is said to have committed rape upon the victim and she was forced to have sexual relation with other.
He further submits that evidence during the trial adduced by the victim was quite consistent with the statement of victim recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.

He further Md. Istiyak Queresi @ Md. Istiyak ... vs The State Of Bihar on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23471780/

sentences.text: He further submits that the statement of victim's sister is quite consistent with the story of prosecution.
The victim was minor on the date of alleged Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.3539 of 2024(11) dt.08-09-2025 occurrence.
He further submits that victim was having no choice being minor who has taken shelter as she was in the custody of appellant.
The manner in which FIR was lodged is quite evident that how the assistance is rendered to the victim as victim expressed to join particular shelter, leaving the custody of appellant.
He further submits that there is no reason to falsely implicate the appellant who has provided shelter to the traceless victim and her younger sister.

He further submits that DNA test cannot absolve the appellant from conviction and sentence under the said sections in the light of manner of occurrence and accusation made against the appellant which is quite evident from the story of prosecution which relates back to three years from the date of lodging of FIR.

He further submits that P.W. 5 (I.O.), has recorded the statements of victim and her younger sister under Sections 161 and their statements have also been recorded under 164 of Cr.P.C. and there is nothing on record to discredit the earlier statements of victim and her younger sister.
The entire prosecution story and other materials are quite supportive with regard to the allegation made by the victim.

He further submits that statements of victim and her younger sister are recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. and their evidence adduced during trial are quire intact and victim and her sister Patna High Court CR.
APP (SJ) No.3539 of 2024(11) dt.08-09-2025 can be categorized as sterling witnesses in the present case and, hence, appellant is not entitled to get suspension of sentence and grant of bail.

7. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, statement of victim adduced during the course of trial in consonance with the statement of victim recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. are quite consistent as well as other material available on record, I am not inclined to enlarge the appellant on bail for the present.
Accordingly, prayer for bail of the appellant is hereby rejected.
8. However, if the appeal is not taken up for final hearing within six months, the appellant may renew his prayer for bail.
9. The Registry is directed to list this case on 11.11.2025 for final hearing within a priority of five cases.
